question: What is the maximum gross monthly income, in dollars, for a household of 3 to qualify for SNAP in Colorado?

answer: 61050 per year (5088 per month)

question: Which categories of people can qualify for WIC in Colorado?
answer: Pregnant people; postpartum people (up to 6 months after pregnancy ends); breastfeeding people (up to 12 months after birth); infants; children up to age 5. Applicants must live in Colorado and meet income guidelines unless categorically eligible.
supporting_quote: Search summary: Colorado WIC serves income-eligible pregnant women, postpartum women, breastfeeding mothers, infants and children up to age 5; mothers of babies up to 6 months and mothers breastfeeding babies up to 12 months are included.

question: Is a household that receives SNAP, Medicaid, or TANF automatically income-eligible for WIC in Colorado?
answer: Yes. Households receiving TANF, Health First Colorado (Medicaid), SNAP or FDPIR are categorically (automatically) eligible for WIC, so the income test is waived. Household members with WIC-eligible categories still must meet the category requirement.
supporting_quote: Search summary: Families receiving TANF, Health First Colorado, SNAP or FDPIR are automatically eligible for WIC.

question: Can a renter whose heat is included in their rent qualify for LEAP if they do not live in subsidized housing?
answer: Yes. Per CDHS, renters can qualify if heat is included in rent and they do not live in subsidized housing. A recent rent receipt showing heat is included is typically required.

question: Who can apply for Colorado Works cash assistance (what are the eligibility criteria)?
answer: Colorado residents with low income who are pregnant or have a dependent child under 18 in their care, who meet the income limits, who cooperate with child support services when the other parent is absent, and who seek work or join a work activity.
supporting_quote: Search summary: Colorado Works requires pregnancy or a dependent child under 18, income limits, cooperation with child support services if the other parent is absent, and work participation.

question: What maximum annual family income does the Colorado Works page state for eligibility?
answer: Not found. Colorado Works uses a monthly Need Standard by family size rather than an annual income cap. One unverified third-party guide lists 421 per month for a family of 3.

question: What are the ways to apply for Colorado Works?

question: What are the state-level income boundaries for CCCAP eligibility (the minimum poverty-guideline percentage counties must serve, and the maximum as a percent of state median income)?
answer: Minimum: counties must serve families at or below 185% of the federal poverty guideline. Maximum: 85% of state median income.
supporting_quote: Search summary: counties must serve families at or below 185% of the federal poverty guideline; no county can serve families above 85% of the state median income. One 2015 state document says 165%, which appears to be an error.

question: Does each Colorado county set its own CCCAP eligibility requirements within the state boundaries?
answer: Yes. Counties set their own income maximums and other program conditions within the state boundaries, and some counties have waitlists or enrollment freezes.
supporting_quote: Search summary: counties set individual income maximums for eligibility along with other program requirements; some counties use higher entry thresholds for new applicants, others lower.
